body: The spec is generally coherent, but a few claims are asserted rather than established. (1) The musician definition — '≥1 year of musical training' — is a strikingly low bar for a group expected to show functional connectivity differences from trained non-musicians; the literature on musician brains typically uses multi-year, currently-practicing musicians, and a single year of childhood lessons may dilute any effect toward the null. This cutoff is treated as fixed ('the strict ≥1 year threshold') without justification, and the sensitivity analysis sweeps p-value thresholds, not the grouping threshold, so the most consequential arbitrary choice in the design goes unexamined. (2) The power claim (≥0.80 to detect d≈0.5 at 50/group) is stated as an assumption but is never derived, and for connectome-wide comparisons with FDR/NBS correction the effective power depends on the number of connections and the correlation structure among tests — a medium-effect claim at the edge level is much weaker than it sounds. (3) User Story 3's sensitivity scenario lists 'thresholds of, 0.05, and 0.10' — the 0.01 level named in FR-005 appears to have been dropped, so the spec contradicts its own requirement. (4) Matching and regression are offered interchangeably ('match or regress out') though they have different failure modes with SES and motion; the spec should commit to one and specify how regression residuals enter the group comparison. (5) The assumption that self-reported training history is reliable 'without requiring additional validation steps' is asserted, not established, and it underwrites the entire grouping.

A well-drafted spec on the whole — the pipeline logic is coherent and the observational-vs-causal framing in the assumptions is refreshingly honest. But a few seams show. First, the original question promises a correlation with 'musical aptitude,' and the spec quietly drops it: every requirement (FR-004, US-3) keys only on 'years of musical training,' with no variable, entity field, or acceptance scenario for aptitude. The research question as validated includes a term the spec cannot measure. Second, SC-005 is vacuous by the spec's own logic: US-1 mandates that subjects with missing training history 'are excluded from the final analysis set,' so 100% of the final dataset will have valid labels by construction — a 90% criterion measures nothing. Third, there is a scope mismatch between the multiple-comparison machinery and the hypothesis: FR-003 restricts tests to 'connections within auditory, motor, and executive control networks,' yet the NBS justification repeatedly defends 'family-wise error across the massive multiple-comparison space inherent in whole-brain connectivity.' Either the analysis is network-restricted (and NBS over a restricted edge set needs its own justification) or it is whole-brain (and FR-003 misstates the test space). Finally, the ≥1-year musician threshold deserves a note: one year of training is a very light criterion by the standards of this literature, and the sensitivity analysis (FR-005) sweeps p-value thresholds but never the group-definition threshold — arguably the more consequential arbitrary cutoff in the design.
